summary: No publisher model card or system card exists for Raptor mini. GitHub owner documentation described it as an experimental VS Code Copilot model and catalog context identifies it as a fine-tuned GPT-5 mini, so this digest points to the base gpt-5-mini folder while warning that Raptor itself was not evaluated publicly.

capabilities.text: GitHub's changelog described Raptor mini as an experimental Copilot model rolling out in Visual Studio Code.
The changelog said the model could be selected for chat, ask, edit, and agent modes in VS Code.
GitHub supported-models documentation identified the lineage as a fine-tuned GPT-5 mini.

limitations.text: No publisher system card or model card exists for Raptor mini itself.
The owner documentation does not report Raptor-specific benchmark scores or safety evaluations.
The changelog documents Visual Studio Code availability, not Copilot CLI availability.
Base GPT-5 mini materials do not evaluate the Raptor fine-tune, and fine-tuning can change behavior.

practical_implications.text: GitHub retired the model on 2026-09-01; remaining guidance is historical and lineage-focused.
Use the gpt-5-mini folder only as incomplete base-model context.
Do not infer Raptor-specific safety or benchmark behavior from missing documentation.
Treat old Raptor mini outputs as preview-era VS Code behavior, not as a current CLI model.

coverage_notes: This digest covers GitHub's Raptor mini changelog and the supported-models lineage note. Because no publisher card exists, evaluations and safety_findings are empty and limitations emphasize the absence of Raptor-specific evidence.
